translations.literal: When after retirement he fell ill he had monks shave his crown; when he died he left instructions to his sons to bury him by the barbarian law in a pagoda, without a mound or trees, hoping to be classed with the black-robed clergy — public opinion ridiculed this.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired he fell ill and had monks shave his crown. When he died he instructed his sons to bury him according to Buddhist custom in a pagoda, without a mound or trees, hoping to be counted among the clergy. Public opinion ridiculed this.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：祿山狂悖已顯，玄宗寵任無疑，見素知國危，陳廟算，直言極諫，而君不從，獨正犯難，而人不咎，出生入死，善始令終者鮮矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Lushan's madness and perversity were already manifest, and Xuanzong's favor and trust were beyond doubt. Jiansu knew the state was in peril, set forth the altars' strategy, and spoke frankly with utmost remonstrance, yet the ruler did not follow; he alone upheld rectitude and braved hardship, yet men did not blame him — those who pass through birth and death and achieve a good beginning and fine end are few.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Lushan's madness and perversity were already plain, and Xuanzong's favor was beyond question. Jiansu knew the state was in peril, set forth the strategy of the altars, and remonstrated with utmost frankness, yet the ruler would not listen. He alone upheld rectitude and braved hardship, yet men did not blame him. Those who pass through birth and death and achieve a good beginning and a fine end are few indeed.

sentences.zh: 時論以見素取容於國忠，無言匡大政。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that Jiansu sought accommodation with Guozhong and spoke no word to rectify great policy.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that Jiansu sought accommodation with Guozhong and never spoke to rectify major policy.

sentences.zh: 且國忠恃內戚，弄重權，沮林甫奸豪，取其大位，若見素之孤直，豈許取容？

translations.literal: Moreover Guozhong relied on inner kinship, wielded heavy power, obstructed the treacherous hero Lin Fu and took his great post — if Jiansu were truly isolated and upright, how could he be permitted to seek accommodation?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guozhong relied on imperial kinship, wielded heavy power, blocked the treacherous hero Li Linfu, and took his great post. If Jiansu were truly isolated and upright, how could he have been allowed to seek accommodation?

sentences.zh: 蓋禍胎已成，政柄久紊，見素入相余年，言不從而難作，雖有周、孔之才，其能匡救者乎？

translations.literal: For the womb of disaster had already formed, government power had long been disordered, Jiansu entered the chancellorship for more than a year yet his words were not followed and calamity arose — even with the talents of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, could he have rescued and restored?
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of disaster had already been sown and government power had long been in disorder. Jiansu served as chancellor for more than a year, but his words went unheeded and calamity followed. Even with the talents of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, how could he have rescued the state?

sentences.zh: 諤才辯，顗儉約，雅符積善之慶矣。

translations.literal: E was talented in debate, Yan frugal and abstemious — both aptly matched the blessing of accumulated goodness.
translations.idiomatic: E was talented in debate and Yan frugal and abstemious — both aptly reflected the blessing of accumulated virtue.

sentences.zh: 圓守文之士，非禦侮之才。

translations.literal: Yuan was a man who upheld written culture, not one with talent to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a man who upheld literary culture, not one with talent to repel invasion.

sentences.zh: 渙才兼行聞，命與時會。

translations.literal: Huan's talent and conduct were jointly renowned; his mandate met the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was renowned for both talent and conduct, and his appointment came at the right moment.

sentences.zh: 發言上沃主意，遽致顯榮；

translations.literal: In speech he enriched the sovereign's intentions above and swiftly attained conspicuous glory;
translations.idiomatic: His words enriched the emperor's thinking and swiftly won him conspicuous glory;

sentences.zh: 當官屢為吏欺，終及竄逐。

translations.literal: in office he was repeatedly deceived by subordinate officials and in the end was driven into exile.
translations.idiomatic: yet in office he was repeatedly deceived by subordinate officials and in the end was driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 所謂可與適道，未可與權。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by one who may be joined in following the Way but not in wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by one who may be joined in following the Way but not in wielding power.

sentences.zh: 縱忠於國，能於官，孝於家，三者備矣，孰能繼之？

translations.literal: Zong was loyal to the state, capable in office, and filial in the family — all three were complete; who could succeed him?
translations.idiomatic: Zong was loyal to the state, capable in office, and filial in the family. All three virtues were complete in him. Who could succeed him?

sentences.zh: 鴻漸有衛社之功，非幹城之責，時以任崔旰為非，則不然矣。

translations.literal: Hongjian had merit in guarding the altars of state but not the responsibility of defending the walls; men of the time regarded appointing Cui Gan as wrong — this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian had merit in guarding the altars of state but not the responsibility of defending the walls. Men of the time regarded his appointment of Cui Gan as wrong — but that is not so.

sentences.zh: 且旰南拒貞節，北敗獻誠，宜以懷來，未可力制，終致歸國，豈非臧謀？

translations.literal: Moreover Gan resisted Zhenjie to the south and defeated Xian Cheng to the north; he should be won by embrace and could not be controlled by force; in the end he caused return to the state — was this not a good plan?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Gan resisted Bo Zhenjie to the south and defeated Xian Cheng to the north. He should be won by conciliation and could not be controlled by force alone. In the end he brought the region back to the state. Was this not sound strategy?

sentences.zh: 向討之，即為劇賊矣。

translations.literal: Had one attacked him, he would at once have become a fierce bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Had the court attacked him, he would at once have become a fierce rebel.

sentences.zh: 然事佛僥福，朋勢取容，非君子之道焉。

translations.literal: Yet in serving the Buddha to seek fortune, forming factions and power to gain accommodation — this is not the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in serving the Buddha to seek fortune and forming factions to gain accommodation — this was not the way of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：玄宗失德，祿山肆逆。

translations.literal: The encomium states: Xuanzong lost virtue, and Lushan unleashed rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Xuanzong lost virtue, and Lushan unleashed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 見素竭節，諸公協力。

translations.literal: Jiansu exhausted his integrity, and the various lords joined their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu gave his utmost loyalty, and these lords joined their strength together.
